office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, energy policy, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Third-term Democratic incumbent and House Majority Whip Alex Ramel faces Orcas Island stone mason Joseph Segault, a newcomer with no party preference, after Ramel took 68% of the primary vote in Whatcom County. Ramel voted for the 2026 income tax and is voting no on all statewide initiatives; Segault opposes rising taxes and wants the income tax put to a public vote.

candidates.summary: Third-term State Representative and House Majority Whip, a former clean-energy organizer focused on climate, housing and progressive revenue.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S3][S5][S6]
Co-sponsored and voted for the 2025 limit on residential rent and fee increases [S7]
Says he is voting no on all statewide initiatives, including I-645, I-1 and I-638 [S1]
Names building decarbonization and rent stabilization among his proudest accomplishments [S8]

taxes.basis: Voted yes on ESSB 6346, EHB 2081 and ESSB 5814; supports the high-earner tax, opposes I-645 and requires any new tax to be progressive.

housing.basis: Co-sponsored and voted for the EHB 1217 rent cap, calls rent stabilization a top accomplishment and cites affordable-housing funding.

climate.basis: Campaigns on 'bold climate action'; record on building decarbonization and clean-energy siting.

social.basis: Says he is '100% pro-choice' and is voting no on all statewide initiatives, including I-638.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296 on House passage and final passage and is voting no on I-1.

tech.basis: Would allow data-center construction while keeping energy costs off the state and neighboring ratepayers.

experience.basis: Third term and House Majority Whip, facing a political newcomer.

candidates.summary: Orcas Island stone mason and political newcomer with no party preference, running against rising taxes and cost of living.
highlights: Says increased taxes and living costs are pushing people out of local communities [S1][S2]
Says the income tax on millionaire households should go to a vote of the people [S2]
Says restrictive zoning makes housing less affordable and more homes are needed [S2]

taxes.basis: Opposes rising taxes on families and would put the income tax to a public vote; does not state a position on repeal.

spending.basis: Says it is unclear why state budgets are 'totally bloated'; no specific proposals.

housing.basis: Blames restrictive zoning for housing costs and says more homes need to be built.

experience.basis: Political newcomer with no listed elected or professional experience, running as an independent.
